source.title: ZC-Swish: Stabilizing Deep BN-Free Networks for Edge and Micro-Batch Applications

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: Reports training accuracy for randomly initialized CIFAR-100 convolutional networks trained with AdamW, bearing on whether the tested recipe reaches near-zero training error.
record.gate_note: The depth-scaling table reports test accuracy only, so those values do not establish training-error changes with depth. The depth-16 table reports best training accuracy by activation.
record.test_reason: Table 1 measures training accuracy in randomly initialized CIFAR-100 convolutional networks, bearing on V1 in a new, deliberately destabilized training setting. The activation comparison does not directly test V2–V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' conclusion: ZC-Swish performs comparably at depth 8, leads the single-seed depth-16 test comparison and mean depth-16 training accuracy, and collapses with the other activations at depth 32. However, improved stability is not consistent across seeds: ZC-Swish has lower mean test accuracy and higher variability than Swish in the three-seed experiment. The authors acknowledge the limited training budget and describe the results as a controlled proof of concept.
record.recipe_differences: Uses random initialization and gradient training on CIFAR-100, but uses AdamW, a custom BN-free PlainNet, default uniform initialization, and a 30-epoch budget; it does not reproduce the cited studies' recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: Activation and depth affect reported outcomes. Depth-16 training accuracy varies by activation; depth-scaling results report test accuracy, with all activations collapsing at depth 32.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 2 reports best test accuracy across depths 8, 16, and 32; all activations approach chance performance at depth 32.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation choice affects test performance as depth increases in BN-free CIFAR-100 PlainNets under a fixed 30-epoch recipe. Test accuracy alone does not establish V3's training-error degradation.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 5.1 reports a Swish training-loss spike above 130 near epoch 13, followed by partial recovery, while ZC-Swish avoids the spike.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation choice affects transient training instability in this recipe. Without a measured stability threshold or curvature trajectory, this does not test V5.

record.code_released: not stated (the paper says the full system code is publicly available on GitHub but gives no URL in the supplied text)
record.problems: The depth-16 primary experiment uses three seeds and reports large standard deviations. Depth-scaling results use one seed and 30 epochs. The authors state that compute limits constrained epochs, seeds, and hyperparameter searches; depth-32 results may reflect insufficient training, default initialization, or no residual connections. Evaluation is restricted to CIFAR-100.
record.rows_left_out: Depth-scaling results in Table 2 and Figure 3 report test accuracy, not training accuracy or training error, so they were not extracted as rows for V1. No other reported results measure a tested version's named behavior.

untested.parts: CIFAR-10, corrupted or random labels, SGD or Adam recipes, model-size comparisons, and whether longer or less regularized training reaches near-zero error.
Teacher-student ReLU problems, spurious local minima, and the effect of adding student neurons.
Training-error degradation across depths in batch-normalized networks, matched identity-shortcut controls, very deep plain tanh networks, and Fixup.
Comparisons of initialization schemes, initialization-dependent training speed or depth, and orthogonal versus Gaussian weights or convolution kernels.
Initial stability thresholds, learning-rate sweeps, curvature or sharpness trajectories, and threshold-dependent recovery or divergence.
Matched BN versus no-BN comparisons of training speed or learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source. V1 explicitly allows substantial training error under some regularized or shortened recipes, so these results qualify its applicability rather than directly contradict its sufficiently trained-network claim. The supplied text does not provide readable training-error comparisons across depths.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test CIFAR-10, corrupted or random labels, SGD or Adam without decoupled weight decay, smaller-model comparisons, or early stopping.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems and student width relative to teacher width are not studied.

Does not compare BN and identity shortcuts or report training error across depths; it uses BN-free PlainNets without residual connections. Does not test Fixup or special initialization on deep plain tanh networks.
Does not compare activation-matched, orthogonal, or Gaussian initializations, or measure signal and gradient propagation across layers.
Does not study learning rates above a stability limit, curvature, sharpness, or recovery from a loss increase.
Does not compare batch normalization with no normalization for training speed or learning-rate tolerance, or test Fixup.

tranche.reason: Reports training accuracy bearing on V1 in a new setting: deliberately destabilized CIFAR-100 PlainNets trained with AdamW for 30 epochs. It does not reproduce the original training recipes.

source_check.notes: Training accuracies are best-epoch means across three seeds; extended training and improved initialization remain untested. The paper states that code is publicly available, contrary to the pack's code=n, but supplies no repository URL in this text.
